A conjecture on a tight norm inequality in the finite-dimensional lpl_{p}

A. S. Holevo    A. V. Utkin Affiliation: Steklov Mathematical Institute, RAS, Moscow, Russia
Abstract

We suggest a tight inequality for norms in dd-dimensional space lpl_{p} which has simple formulation but appears hard to prove. We give a proof for d=3d=3 and provide a detailed numerical check for d≤200d\leq 200 confirming the conjecture. An unusual feature is the “phase transition” in the constant of the inequality, depending on the dimension dd and the parameter pp. We conclude with a brief survey of solutions for kin problems which anyhow concern minimization of the output entropy of certain quantum channel and rely upon the symmetry properties of the problem.

Key words and phrases: lpl_{p}-norm, Rényi entropy, tight inequality, maximization of a convex function.

1 Formulation of the problem

Quantum information theory suggests a variety of optimization problems most of which are hard to solve analytically. For problems such as computation of the quantum channel capacity or accessible information the mathematical difficulty is finding a global maximum of a convex function. The problem considered in the present note arose in connection with the computation of accessible information for the ensemble of “quantum pyramid” (see [4]) in [8]. However it can be naturally formulated as optimization problem in dd-dimensional Banach space lpl_{p} without any reference to quantum information science.

Let d≥3d\geq 3 (the case d=2d=2 is trivial) and consider the (d−1)−(d-1)-dimensional hyperplane

L={𝐱=(x1,…,xd)∈ℝd:x1+⋯+xd=0}.L=\left\{\mathbf{x}=(x_{1},\dots,x_{d})\in\mathbb{R}^{d}:x_{1}+\dots+x_{d}=0\right\}.

We conjecture the following tight inequalities: For α≥1\alpha\geq 1

‖𝐱‖2​α≤M​(d,α)1/2​α​‖𝐱‖2,𝐱∈L;\left\|\mathbf{x}\right\|_{2\alpha}\leq M\left(d,\alpha\right)^{1/2\alpha}\left\|\mathbf{x}\right\|_{2},\quad\mathbf{x}\in L; (1)

For 0<α<10<\alpha<1

‖𝐱‖2​α≥M​(d,α)1/2​α​‖𝐱‖2,𝐱∈L,\left\|\mathbf{x}\right\|_{2\alpha}\geq M\left(d,\alpha\right)^{1/2\alpha}\left\|\mathbf{x}\right\|_{2},\quad\mathbf{x}\in L, (2)

where the constant M⁡(d,α)M\left(d,\alpha\right) is exact and is defined as follows:

M⁡(d,α)={21−α,d≤d⁡(α);d−α​[(d−1)α+(d−1)1−α],d>d⁡(α)M\left(d,\alpha\right)=\left\{\begin{array}[]{cc}2^{1-\alpha},&d\leq d(\alpha);\\ d^{-\alpha}\left[\left(d-1\right)^{\alpha}+\left(d-1\right)^{1-\alpha}\right],&d>d(\alpha)\end{array}\right. (3)

when α>1/2,\alpha>1/2, and M⁡(d,α)=21−αM\left(d,\alpha\right)=2^{1-\alpha} when α≤1/2\alpha\leq 1/2 (in particular, ‖𝐱‖1≥2​‖𝐱‖2,𝐱∈L\left\|\mathbf{x}\right\|_{1}\geq\sqrt{2}\left\|\mathbf{x}\right\|_{2},\,\mathbf{x}\in L). Here the value d⁡(α)d(\alpha) is the largest root of the equation

21−α=d−α​[(d−1)α+(d−1)1−α].2^{1-\alpha}=d^{-\alpha}\left[\left(d-1\right)^{\alpha}+\left(d-1\right)^{1-\alpha}\right]. (4)

In the case d≤d⁡(α)d\leq d(\alpha) the equality in the conjectured inequalities (1), (2) is attained for x1=−x2=1/2,xj=0x_{1}=-x_{2}=1/\sqrt{2},\,x_{j}=0, j≥3;j\geq 3; in the case d>d⁡(α)d>d(\alpha) – for x1=d−1d,xj=−1(d−1)​d,j≥2,x_{1}=\sqrt{\frac{d-1}{d}},\,x_{j}=-\sqrt{\frac{1}{\left(d-1\right)d}},\,j\geq 2, (and for all permutations and total change of sign of such OPENxj).x_{j}). Correspondingly, we speak of the maximizers of the first and second types.

For α>1/2\alpha>1/2 the equation (4) has exactly two roots: d=2d=2 and d=d⁡(α)>2.d=d(\alpha)>2. The function d⁡(α)d(\alpha) is monotonically decreasing from +∞+\infty for α=1/2\alpha=1/2 to d⁡(1∓0)=6.47​…d(1\mp 0)=6.47..., which is the solution of the equation

log⁡(d/2)=d−2d​log⁡(d−1),\log(d/2)=\frac{d-2}{d}\log(d-1), (5)

and then to d⁡(∞)=2.d(\infty)=2. The equation (5) is obtained by taking the logarithmic derivative of (4) with respect to α\alpha at α=1.\alpha=1. Another important point is α=2\alpha=2 for which d⁡(2)=3.d(2)=3. For all α>2\alpha>2 it holds d⁡(α)<3,d(\alpha)<3, and since the dimension dd takes only integer values 3,4,…,3,4,\dots, the quantity M⁡(d,α)M\left(d,\alpha\right) is then always given by the second option in (3).

The plot of the function α→d⁡(α),α>0,\alpha\rightarrow d(\alpha),\,\alpha>0, is given in Fig. 1.

The proof of the conjectured inequalities reduces to the following problem:

For d≥3d\geq 3 and α≥1\alpha\geq 1 show that

M⁡(d,α)=max⁡∑j=1d𝐱⁡|xj|2​αM(d,\alpha)=\max_{\mathbf{x}}\sum_{j=1}^{d}\left|x_{j}\right|^{2\alpha} (6)

under the constraints

∑j=1d|xj|2=1,∑j=1dxj=0,\sum_{j=1}^{d}\left|x_{j}\right|^{2}=1,\quad\sum_{j=1}^{d}x_{j}=0, (7)

with the maximizers described above.

For α<1\alpha<1 the maximum in (6) is replaced by the minimum.

For 𝐱∈ℝd\mathbf{x\in}\mathbb{R}^{d} with ‖𝐱‖2=1\left\|\mathbf{x}\right\|_{2}=1 introduce the probability distribution P𝐱=(|x1|2,…,|xd|2)P_{\mathbf{x}}=\left(\left|x_{1}\right|^{2},\dots,\left|x_{d}\right|^{2}\right) . Then for α≠1\alpha\neq 1 the problem can be reformulated in terms of α\alpha-Rényi entropy Hα​(P𝐱)=(1−α)−1​log​∑j=1d|xj|2​α:H_{\alpha}(P_{\mathbf{x}})=\left(1-\alpha\right)^{-1}\log\sum_{j=1}^{d}\left|x_{j}\right|^{2\alpha}:

min𝐱∈L⁡Hα​(P𝐱)={log⁡2,d≤d⁡(α);(1−α)−1​log⁡d−α​[(d−1)α+(d−1)1−α],d>d⁡(α)\min_{\mathbf{x}\in L}H_{\alpha}(P_{\mathbf{x}})=\left\{\begin{array}[]{cc}\log 2,&d\leq d(\alpha);\\ \left(1-\alpha\right)^{-1}\log d^{-\alpha}\left[\left(d-1\right)^{\alpha}+\left(d-1\right)^{1-\alpha}\right],&d>d(\alpha)\end{array}\right.

The case α→1\alpha\rightarrow 1 corresponds to minimization of the Shannon entropy H⁡(P𝐱)H(P_{\mathbf{x}}) considered in [8] in connection with the problem of accessible information for ensemble of “quantum pyramid” [4]. Going to the limit and taking into account that 6<d⁡(1±0)<76<d(1\pm 0)<7 amounts to

min𝐱∈L⁡H⁡(P𝐱)={log⁡2,d≤6;log⁡d−d−2d​log⁡(d−1),d≥7.\min_{\mathbf{x}\in L}H(P_{\mathbf{x}})=\left\{\begin{array}[]{cc}\log 2,&d\leq 6;\\ \log d-\frac{d-2}{d}\log(d-1),&d\geq 7.\end{array}\right.

3 Numerical verification

Theoretical background.

We consider both cases α>1\alpha>1 and 0<α<10<\alpha<1.

The Lagrange method is useful to make the computation faster, since the constraints (8) yield O⁡(d2)O(d^{2}) one-dimensional optimization problems in certain dimension dd.

We consider the maximization problem for the function

For the numerical verification of hypothesis (2) (with α∈(0,1)\alpha\in(0,1)), the algorithm description should involve finding the minimum of the function f⁡(t)f(t) from the algorithm instead of its maximum.

Complexity.

Instead of optimizing over ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d}, the algorithm reduces the problem to O⁡(d2)O(d^{2}) one-dimensional optimizations, making verification feasible for dd up to several hundred.

Expected outcome.

The behavior of Mnum​(d)M_{\text{num}}(d) depends on α\alpha as follows:

  • •

    For α>1\alpha>1: there exists a critical dimension d⁡(α)d(\alpha) such that

    Mnum​(d)≈{21−α,d<d⁡(α)d−α​((d−1)α+(d−1)1−α),d≥d⁡(α)M_{\text{num}}(d)\approx\begin{cases}2^{1-\alpha},&d<d(\alpha)\\ d^{-\alpha}\big((d-1)^{\alpha}+(d-1)^{1-\alpha}\big),&d\geq d(\alpha)\end{cases}
  • •

    Mnum​(d)≈{d−α​((d−1)α+(d−1)1−α),d<d⁡(α)21−α,d≥d⁡(α)M_{\text{num}}(d)\approx\begin{cases}d^{-\alpha}\big((d-1)^{\alpha}+(d-1)^{1-\alpha}\big),&d<d(\alpha)\\ 2^{1-\alpha},&d\geq d(\alpha)\end{cases}

    For 0<α≤0.50<\alpha\leq 0.5: Mnum​(d)≈21−αM_{\text{num}}(d)\approx 2^{1-\alpha} for all dd.

The critical dimension satisfies (5)

21−α=d​(α)−α​((d⁡(α)−1)α+(d⁡(α)−1)1−α).2^{1-\alpha}=d(\alpha)^{-\alpha}\big((d(\alpha)-1)^{\alpha}+(d(\alpha)-1)^{1-\alpha}\big).

Verification results.

The algorithm confirms the hypothesis for all tested dimensions within tolerance ϵ\epsilon, showing perfect agreement with the theoretical predictions. Specifically, numerical verification was performed for α=0.05\alpha=0.05, 0.20.2, 0.450.45, 0.50.5, 0.550.55, 0.70.7, 0.950.95, 1.011.01, 1.11.1, 1.51.5, and 22 across dimensions d=3d=3 through 200200. In each case, the computed maximum Mnum​(d,α)M_{\text{num}}(d,\alpha) coincides (within the prescribed tolerance) with the conjectured value. The correspondence holds for every tested pair (α,d)(\alpha,d), confirming the validity of the structural hypothesis over the investigated range.

4 Discussion

Here we give references to solutions of several problems akin to our conjecture. All cases one way or another concern minimization of the output entropy of certain quantum channel (normalized completely positive map) and rely upon the symmetry properties of the problem.

In [9] Lieb gave a solution of the Wehrl conjecture which can be reformulated as a conjecture about the minimal output entropy of the measurement (quantum-classical) channel associated with the Glauber’s coherent states with the underlying Heisenberg group, and generalized the conjecture to SU(2) group. The solution was based on the sharp versions of Young’s and Hausdorff-Young inequalities in the classical harmonic analysis. In [10] Lieb and Solovej proved the Wehrl-type entropy conjecture for symmetric SU(N) coherent states and suggested a similar conjecture for larger class of Lie groups and their representation (for further progress in this direction see [5] and the references therein). In [10] the authors used the “universal cloning channel” and established minimization for arbitrary concave function of the output distribution (the majorization).

Another relevant case is the solution of the Gaussian optimizers conjecture for the classical capacity of bosonic Gaussian channels by Giovannetti, Holevo and Garcia-Patron [1]. The result for the minimal Wehrl entropy problem can be obtained from a special limiting case of this [2]. For one mode Gaussian measurement channels the aforementioned conjecture was settled in [6], [7]. In that case certain generalizations of the logarithmic Sobolev inequality were used. In all these cases the symmetry group was a Lie group, while a generalization to the case of Weyl system, associated with arbitrary (not necessarily continuous) locally compact Abelian group paired with its dual, was elaborated by Zelenov [12].

We surmise that the hypothesis of the present paper could be regarded as a discrete relative of the aforementioned problems, within the context of the symmetric group and its standard representation. It seems that maximizers in the problem (6) can play the role of a discrete analogue of coherent state vectors. However, what is unusual as compared to problems with continuous symmetry groups is the presence of two types of maximizers and a “phase transition” between them.
